analysis.title: "Bullish On The Diffusion Of Intelligence" But Citadel Securities Bond Boss Warns About Rising Real Price Of Capital
key_insights: 49bp of September's 54bp rise in 10y yields came from real yields, which finished close to 3%. Breakevens widened only 5bp. Investors are demanding a higher return after inflation rather than more inflation protection.

The move is consistent with markets repricing the strength and persistence of growth and the real rates needed to accommodate it. Procyclical fiscal easing, loose financial conditions and the AI-investment boom support strong demand.

Government borrowing supports activity but adds to the debt markets must absorb, with AI competing for capital alongside it. Financing investment alongside persistent deficits requires more saving or a higher real return.

Shah is wary of calling a durable top in yields just because inflation improves, and equally wary of extrapolating the sell-off indefinitely. Further upside requires fresh repricing of growth, policy, or term premia.
Rate-sensitive sectors are strained. US 30-year fixed mortgage rates rose 25bp last week to average 7.28%, the largest weekly increase since October 2022.

Stable breakevens are read as an expectation that the Fed will deliver the higher real rates needed to contain inflation, not as evidence inflation is solved. August core PCE rose 0.2% MoM but annual core inflation stayed at 3.0%, and September manufacturing ISM prices-paid jumped 6.8 points to 77.9.
Markets are discounting 3-4 further hikes this cycle, which Shah considers reasonable given sticky inflation, resilient growth and accommodative financial conditions.

Fiscal support and strategic AI investment make parts of demand less rate-sensitive. De-globalisation and physical constraints limit the goods disinflation available to offset sticky services inflation.

NY Fed's Williams said AI-related demand is still outrunning supply, with higher input costs starting to affect other products while housing inflation has eased. Further tightening only requires inflation to decline too slowly while demand stays resilient.

Chair Warsh has stepped back from forward guidance and faces a market signalling a higher destination for policy. Confirmation in the data would give the Fed reason to validate it, though not necessarily at the same pace.
The AI boom can broaden while returns become more uneven. Value can accrue to customers, businesses embedding AI in workflows, and providers of compute and distribution, as well as model developers.

Bain's latest report shows falling token prices offset by more intensive usage and broader deployment, so cheaper intelligence need not mean a smaller compute bill. Cheaper tokens can still pressure producers' pricing power.

Shah sees standalone frontier model development as harder to monetise sustainably than the broader compute complex, given the cost of funding successive generations while competing with cheaper open-weight models. He is most bullish on hyperscalers.

Microsoft expanded Copilot with new models from OpenAI and Anthropic and separated subscription-based everyday AI from usage-based agentic work, with automatic routing on accuracy, speed and cost. Google reports using Argon agents to improve datacentre memory efficiency.

An estimated one-third of hyperscaler capex is debt-financed this year. The higher real cost of capital makes the timing and reliability of future cash generation more consequential, favouring integrated platforms with existing cash flows and distribution.

market_movers.rationale: Copilot now offers OpenAI and Anthropic models with revised pricing separating subscription from usage-based agentic work. Shah cites it as an example of the customer relationship enduring while the underlying model changes.
Google reports using Argon agents to improve datacentre memory efficiency, cited as a model supporting a larger business rather than carrying the investment case itself.

sector_views.rationale: Economics extend beyond selling model access, and existing cash flows, distribution and multiple monetisation routes matter more as the real cost of capital rises.
Harder to monetise sustainably than the broader compute complex given funding needs and competition from cheaper open-weight models.
30-year mortgage rates at 7.28% squeeze purchasing power in an already weak housing market.

macro_indicators.reading: +54bp, of which 49bp real yield and 5bp breakeven
macro_indicators.interpretation: The sell-off is driven by higher real yields, a demand for higher after-inflation returns.
Real cost of capital is rising with the growth and AI-investment boom.

macro_indicators.indicator: Q2 real private domestic final demand
macro_indicators.interpretation: Strong underlying demand supports higher real rates.
Input price pressure is rising, which argues against easing in inflation.

macro_indicators.reading: payroll miss, negative revisions, softer wages, higher unemployment rate; 3m average +51k
macro_indicators.interpretation: Labor data was weak but the 3m average stays positive, so it does not overturn the strong-demand picture.
Tactical relief on the month, but annual core inflation remains elevated.
Largest weekly increase since October 2022, further pressuring housing.
Shah considers this pricing reasonable given sticky inflation and resilient growth.

trade_ideas.description: Favour integrated hyperscaler platforms over standalone frontier model developers
trade_ideas.rationale: Hyperscaler economics extend beyond selling model access and are better placed to fund capex at a higher real cost of capital.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher real cost of capital, with an estimated one-third of hyperscaler capex debt-financed this year.

risk_factors: Further rise in real yields and term premia if growth, policy, or term premia are repriced.
Sticky services inflation with limited goods disinflation from de-globalisation and physical constraints.
Debt-financed hyperscaler capex (about one-third this year) is more exposed to a higher real cost of capital.
Pricing pressure on model producers from falling token prices and cheaper open-weight models.
Rate-sensitive sectors such as housing are strained by 7.28% mortgage rates.
